authors.name: G. W. F. Hegel
authors.role: German idealist philosopher. Marx took his dialectic and set it on a materialist footing.

authors.name: Karl Marx
authors.role: Founded scientific socialism with Engels. Spent his last decades on Capital.

authors.name: Friedrich Engels
authors.role: Marx's partner for forty years. Edited volumes II and III of Capital after Marx died.

authors.name: Ferdinand Lassalle
authors.role: Founded the General German Workers' Association in 1863. Marx's Critique of the Gotha Programme was written against his legacy.

authors.name: Karl Kautsky
authors.role: Leading theorist of the German SPD and the Second International.

authors.name: G. V. Plekhanov
authors.role: Founder of Russian Marxism and teacher of Lenin's generation; later a leader of the Mensheviks, who opposed the October revolution.

authors.name: V. I. Lenin
authors.role: Led the Bolshevik party and the October Revolution of 1917.

authors.name: Leon Trotsky
authors.role: Chaired the Petrograd Soviet in 1905 and 1917 and organised the Red Army.

authors.name: Rosa Luxemburg
authors.role: Co-founded the Spartacus League. Murdered in Berlin in January 1919.

authors.name: Karl Liebknecht
authors.role: The only deputy to vote against war credits in December 1914. Murdered with Luxemburg in January 1919.

authors.name: N. I. Bukharin
authors.role: Bolshevik theorist and editor of Pravda. Shot in 1938 after the third Moscow trial. In USSR 2089, he lives.

authors.name: Georg Lukács
authors.role: People's commissar in the Hungarian Soviet Republic of 1919. History and Class Consciousness reopened Marx's debt to Hegel.

authors.name: Amadeo Bordiga
authors.role: First leader of the Communist Party of Italy in 1921, and the leading figure of the Italian Communist Left.

authors.name: Baruch Spinoza
authors.role: Dutch philosopher, expelled from Amsterdam's Jewish community in 1656, whose Ethics identifies God with nature. Hegel held that every philosopher must begin from Spinoza.

authors.name: Immanuel Kant
authors.role: Königsberg philosopher whose critical philosophy set the problems that Hegel answered. A century later, Bernstein and the neo-Kantians called for a return to Kant.

authors.name: Ludwig Feuerbach
authors.role: Young Hegelian who turned Hegel's philosophy into a materialism of man and nature. Marx's Theses on Feuerbach and Engels's Ludwig Feuerbach settle accounts with him.

authors.name: Bruno Bauer
authors.role: Young Hegelian theologian and critic of the Gospels, Marx's teacher and friend in Berlin, whom Marx answered in On the Jewish Question and, with Engels, in The Holy Family.

authors.name: Moses Hess
authors.role: Philosopher and socialist who won Engels over to communism in 1842 and worked with Marx in the 1840s; later the author of Rome and Jerusalem (1862), an early work of Zionism.

authors.name: Adam Smith
authors.role: Scottish moral philosopher whose Wealth of Nations founded classical political economy, the starting point of Marx's critique.

authors.name: Thomas Malthus
authors.role: Clergyman and economist whose law of population Marx attacked as an apology for poverty.

authors.name: David Ricardo
authors.role: Stockbroker and economist who carried the labour theory of value further than anyone before Marx.

authors.name: Henri de Saint-Simon
authors.role: French aristocrat who imagined a society run by industrialists and scientists. Engels counted him among the three great utopians.

authors.name: Robert Owen
authors.role: Welsh mill-owner who ran New Lanark as a model factory town and founded communities in Britain and America.

authors.name: Charles Fourier
authors.role: French critic of commerce and of 'civilisation' who planned cooperative communities, the phalansteries.

authors.name: Auguste Blanqui
authors.role: French revolutionary who spent more than thirty years in prison for his conspiracies and insurrections; his followers fought in the Paris Commune.

authors.name: Max Stirner
authors.role: Young Hegelian whose The Ego and Its Own set the individual above every cause. Marx and Engels answered him at great length in The German Ideology.

authors.name: Pierre-Joseph Proudhon
authors.role: French printer who declared that property is theft and was the first to call himself an anarchist. Marx answered his System of Economic Contradictions with The Poverty of Philosophy.

authors.name: Mikhail Bakunin
authors.role: Russian revolutionary who fought Marx for the First International and was expelled from it at the Hague Congress of 1872.

authors.name: Peter Kropotkin
authors.role: Russian prince and geographer, the leading theorist of anarchist communism.

authors.name: Emma Goldman
authors.role: Lithuanian-born American anarchist, deported to Soviet Russia in 1919, who wrote of her disillusionment there.

authors.name: Eduard Bernstein
authors.role: Engels's literary executor, who argued from 1896 that socialism would come by gradual reform. His party rejected the revision, and Luxemburg answered it in Reform or Revolution.

authors.name: Joseph Stalin
authors.role: General Secretary of the Soviet Communist Party from 1922 and ruler of the USSR until his death in 1953; author of the doctrine of socialism in one country.

authors.name: Enver Hoxha
authors.role: Leader of Albania from 1944 until his death in 1985, who broke in turn with Yugoslavia, the Soviet Union and China.

authors.name: Kim Il-sung
authors.role: Leader of North Korea from its founding in 1948 until his death in 1994, and author of its state doctrine of Juche.

authors.name: Mao Zedong
authors.role: Chairman of the Chinese Communist Party, who led it to power in 1949 and ruled the People's Republic of China until his death in 1976.

authors.name: Deng Xiaoping
authors.role: Leader of China from 1978 into the 1990s, who opened its economy to the market under the name of socialism with Chinese characteristics.

authors.name: Xi Jinping
authors.role: General Secretary of the Chinese Communist Party since 2012 and President of China since 2013. His doctrine is written into the party constitution as Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era.

authors.name: Ho Chi Minh
authors.role: Founder of the Indochinese Communist Party in 1930, who declared Vietnam's independence in 1945 and led North Vietnam until his death in 1969.

authors.name: Fidel Castro
authors.role: Lawyer who led the Cuban revolution of 1959, declared it socialist in 1961 and governed Cuba until 2008.

authors.name: Che Guevara
authors.role: Argentine doctor who fought in the Cuban revolution, ran Cuba's national bank and its ministry of industry, and was killed in Bolivia in 1967 while leading a guerrilla campaign.

authors.name: Thomas Sankara
authors.role: Army captain who took power in Upper Volta in 1983, renamed it Burkina Faso, and led it until he was killed in a coup in 1987.

authors.name: Josip Broz Tito
authors.role: Leader of the Yugoslav partisans in the Second World War and of Yugoslavia from 1945 until his death; he broke with Stalin in 1948 and helped found the Non-Aligned Movement.

authors.name: Mikhail Gorbachev
authors.role: Last General Secretary of the Soviet Communist Party, from 1985 to 1991, whose reforms of perestroika and glasnost preceded the end of the Soviet Union.
